content.thinking:
I'm working out the order of the decision outcomes: reject, escalate, return, incomplete, then approve, with the ordering tied to section 2.1. Next I'm looking at the handling of unknown facts in section 2.2, which says a claim cannot be approved if a required fact is unknown, and I'm checking how section 1 defines "incomplete." I'm still trying to find an explicit approval rule.

I'm checking whether an approve rule is needed as a fallback, since the format has no default, and I'm weighing whether section 4.5 (the Finance Director pre-approval carve-out for business-class airfare) could serve as the approval basis.

I'm weighing whether to encode section 4.5 as its own approve rule, even though 4.4 would already escalate any business-class airfare line, so the approve rule would be shadowed. The instructions say to write the SOP as it is and not repair it, so the solver should be the one to surface that conflict, and I'm leaning toward a separate approve rule that the checks can flag.

I'm weighing whether a default approve rule is needed, since nothing in the format says what happens when no rule applies, and section 1 only describes approval as paying the claim. I'm leaning against inventing one and letting the checks surface the gap.

I'm still weighing whether the SOP needs a default approve rule for cases where nothing else applies, since section 2.1 gives an ordering but no fallback. Section 1's "exactly one outcome" line hints at one, but I can't tie it to a specific approve sentence, so I'm leaning toward leaving the gap for the checks to surface.

I'm still undecided on whether to add a default approve rule, since the SOP never says what happens when no other rule applies, and I'm leaning toward leaving that gap for the checks to surface rather than inventing a condition for it.

I'm checking the remaining quirks in the SOP: the 60-versus-61-day boundary looks consistent for whole days, and 4.1's "missing" and "not attached" wording points at the same fact. I can't tell whether the core fills in a default when no rule applies, so I'll leave that gap as it is and note it.

I'm still weighing whether to add a default approve rule. Section 2.2's line about unknown facts implies approval is the norm, but no section says when to approve besides the 4.5 carve-out, so I'm leaning toward leaving that gap unfilled and noting it for the solver.

I'm drafting the rule for the 60-day submission limit, where anything submitted 61 days or more after the earliest expense gets rejected. I'm also starting on the self-approval check, which should reject a claim when the approver is the same employee who submitted it.

I'm writing out the remaining rules: a late submission over 60 days gets rejected, a missing director signature on claims of 5000 or more escalates, a receipt-less line of 75 or more goes back for return, and alcohol lines are returned. I'm also encoding the gift-to-official and business-class airfare escalations, and starting the pre-approved airfare approval rule, which 4.4 would shadow.

I'm settling on the collections for the claim, and I'm not adding any default for empty lines, since the SOP doesn't say anything about that case.

I'm settling on the map entries for this case: cabin class variants like "Business-class" and "first-class" map to business and first, and the category map covers alcohol and gift as needed.

I'm settling the needs list and find nothing to add there: the receipt, pre-approval, and sign-off facts already cover the wording in sections 4.1, 4.5, and 3.3, and the day limit is covered by the 61-day rule.

I'm settling the remaining sections to include, which covers section 1 with the note about approval, and I'm writing the late-submission entry to start the rule list.

I'm settling the wording for the two remaining rules: the 75-dollar receipt requirement, where a missing or unattached receipt means returning the claim, and the anti-bribery escalations for gifts to officials and for business or first-class airfare.

unknowns.text: If any fact required by this procedure is unknown, the claim cannot be approved.

lines.unknown_when_empty: what lines (receipts or expenses) the claim has
lines.text: A claim is a list of lines, one per receipt or expense.

rules.text: Claims must be submitted within 60 days of the earliest expense on them. Reject a claim submitted 61 days or more after its earliest expense.
A claim's approver must not be the employee who submitted it. Reject a self-approved claim.
A claim totalling $5,000 or more needs the Finance Director's sign-off. Without it, escalate.
Every line of $75 or more needs an itemised receipt. If a receipt is missing or has not been attached, return the claim.
Alcohol is not reimbursable. Return any claim with a line for alcohol.
A gift to a government official must be reviewed under the anti-bribery policy. Escalate any claim with such a line.
Business-class and first-class airfare must be reviewed. Escalate any claim with such a line.
Business-class airfare pre-approved in writing by the Finance Director may be approved.

sections.note: Defines the five outcomes and what a claim's lines are (used for the lines list's unknown_when_empty). It says every claim receives exactly one outcome. However, no section says when to approve a claim in general; only 4.5 approves. So a claim that no rule reaches gets no outcome from the SOP as written. I have not added a default approve rule; a person should decide.
Sets the order of outcomes, most severe first: reject, escalate, return, incomplete, approve.
Sets what a rule that might apply, because of an unknown fact, leads to: incomplete (the claim cannot be approved; section 1 defines Incomplete as a required fact not yet established).

Translated as written, as an approve rule. Any line it applies to is also a business-class airfare line under 4.4, which escalates. Escalate is more severe under 2.1, so this rule can never decide a claim. The SOP does not say whether 4.5 is meant as an exception to 4.4, or whether 'may be approved' means anything more. That is for a person to settle.
